alerts.title: EFV neuropsychiatric toxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines state EFV frequently causes neuropsychiatric effects including insomnia, vivid dreams, and dizziness, typically within the first 2-6 weeks of therapy. Patient presents with poor sleep and vivid dreams for several weeks after starting EFV in February 2024 (approximately 23 months ago). While most EFV neuropsychiatric effects occur early, persistent or recurrent symptoms warrant evaluation. Evidence for drug attribution: EFV is a well-documented cause of insomnia and vivid dreams matching this patient's presentation. Evidence against: symptom onset at 23 months is atypical, as most cases manifest within first 2-6 weeks; non-drug causes should be excluded. Guidelines also note suicidality remains a common concern requiring additional assessment; patient denies suicidal ideation.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess symptom severity and duration; consider EFV substitution if symptoms persist or worsen. Screen for depression/anxiety and suicidality. File aDSM form.
